newsitem.title: INDIA: Delhi shares ease to close lower in dull trade.
newsitem.headline: Delhi shares ease to close lower in dull trade.

text.p: Delhi shares closed a shade lower on Wednesday on slackened buying following reports that the Central Board of Trustees of (CBT) employees' provident funds has ruled out investments in shares, brokers said.
The Delhi Stock Exchange's sensitive index closed 1.38 points lower at 783.23 points.

"The CBT's decision to not to allow any investment from provident and pension funds into capital markets came as a shock to speculators and triggered selling," said Suresh Aggarwal of brokers Jai Mata Securities.
Another broker said most players were awaiting the outcome of the Securities and Exchange Board of India's (SEBI) meeting before staking fresh claims.
"Speculators are waiting for the outcome of today's SEBI meeting which is considering a revised carry-forward system," said the broker who asked not to be named.
Trading closed before SEBI's board announced its decisions after a meeting.
TISCO fell 2.0 rupees to 182.05 on selling by foreign funds coupled with profit-taking by speculators, brokers said.
Larsen and Toubro slipped 5.70 rupees to 222.65.
